AccountProfileResponse.description:
Always returned, also before registration has started (`status: not_started`, every requirement
missing), so a client can render the shared Basics & Consent step from this response alone.

accepted.description: Whether any version has been accepted.

current.description:
Whether the current version has been accepted. Initial registration completion requires it. A completed
registration stays complete when a later version makes this `false`; it only signals that a re-consent is
due (a future flow).

accepted.description: Whether any version has been accepted.

current.description:
Whether the current version has been accepted. Initial registration completion requires it. A completed
registration stays complete when a later version makes this `false`; it only signals that a re-consent is
due (a future flow).

missing_requirements.description:
What initial completion still needs, in form order: empty fields, and required consents not
accepted at their current version. Always empty once complete, also after a document version
change (see `consents.*.current`).

status.description:
`not_started`: nothing saved yet. `in_progress`: progress saved, not completed. `complete`:
completion recorded by `completeAccountRegistration`; permanent, also after a later legal
document version change.

AccountProfileResponse.title: AccountProfileResponse

AccountProfileUpdateRequest.description:
Any subset of the registration basics and consent decisions. Omitted fields are unchanged. Nothing is
required while registration is in progress. A save with nothing to persist creates nothing.

accept_privacy.description: Accepts the current Privacy Policy version. Only `true` (`must_be_accepted`).

accept_terms.description: Accepts the current Terms of Service version. Only `true`: required consents cannot be withdrawn here (`must_be_accepted`).

date_of_birth.description:
A real calendar date, not in the future, at least 16 years ago by calendar date (`too_young`
otherwise). Cannot be changed once registration is complete (`immutable`).

full_name.description:
The person's full name (account level; not a role profile's public display name). Trimmed;
`null` clears it while registration is in progress. After completion it can be changed, not cleared.

product_news.description: Optional product news by email: `true` subscribes, `false` withdraws. Never required to complete registration.

AccountProfileUpdateRequest.title: AccountProfileUpdateRequest

AppleAuthRequest.description:
`id_token` is the Apple identity token (a JWT) from Sign in with Apple (Apple JS on the web, iOS). Its
request must have carried the lowercase hex SHA-256 of `nonce`; the raw `nonce` is sent here. Both are
verified by the API and never stored. Nothing else about the person (name, email) is sent or trusted.

id_token.description: Apple identity token. Sensitive: never log or persist it.

nonce.description: The raw nonce whose SHA-256 (lowercase hex) was sent to Apple. Sensitive: never log or persist it.

refresh_token_transport.description:
How to deliver the refresh token (ADR 0010). `body` (mobile) returns it in JSON. `cookie` (web) sets
the `HttpOnly` refresh cookie and requires an allow-listed `Origin` and `x-simplefit-csrf: 1`.

AppleAuthRequest.title: AppleAuthRequest

AppleAuthResponse.description:
The SimpleFit session (same fields as `SessionTokens`) plus `account`: `created` on the first sign-in of
this Apple account, `existing` afterwards. A temporary routing signal for first-time onboarding until
profile/onboarding state is exposed by the API.

access_token.description: Short-lived SimpleFit access token (opaque to clients).

refresh_token.description: Body transport only. Keep it in platform secure storage.

refresh_token_transport.description: Where the refresh token was delivered.

AppleAuthResponse.title: AppleAuthResponse

document_language.description: The `document.language` of the text the coach was shown (an approved variant).

document_version.description: The version from `getMyCoachDataRules` that the coach was shown.

acknowledged_at.description: When the viewer acknowledged that version; `null` until then.

document.description:
The current data-rules text in the requested `language` (`null` while no version is published).
Acknowledge with its `version` and `language`; no `language` (no approved variant in the requested
language): acknowledging is not possible yet.

document_version.description: The coach data-rules version to acknowledge before inviting; `null` while none is configured.

CoachFighterRelationship.description:
A coaching relationship seen by its coach. While `active`: the fighter fields of the accepted disclosure
version. Once `ended`: a stub (dates, who ended it, the fighter's name at the end) and no profile data.

disclosed_fields.description:
The fighter profile fields disclosed under `disclosure_version`, as the backend applies it today: never
more than the fighter accepted. Empty when the relationship has ended or the version is no longer offered.

disclosure_version.description: The disclosure version the fighter accepted (identifier of the approved legal text).

ended_at.description: When the relationship ended; `null` while active.

ended_by.description: Which side ended it; `null` while active.

fighter.description:
The fighter as disclosed to the coach: only the fields listed in `disclosed_fields` carry values, every
other one is `null`. Never contains goals, next fight, weight, height, account name, date of birth, email
or any other personal data. `null` for an ended relationship.

fighter_display_name_at_end.description:
The fighter's display name as it was when the relationship ended (the only fighter data kept
for the coach afterwards); `null` while active.

relationship_id.description: The relationship. The only handle either side uses to address it.

started_at.description: When the fighter accepted the relationship.

status.description: `active` until either side ends it; `ended` is final (a reconnection is a new relationship).

relationships.description: Newest first. Empty when the coach has none (a real, empty roster).

An invitation sent by the viewer. The recipient address is masked; whether it belongs to an account is
never revealed. `expired` is derived from `expires_at`.

never in a URL. Any value that is not a current token answers `410 invitation_unavailable`.

outcome.description:
`created`: a new relationship under the accepted disclosure. `already_connected`: the pair already had an
active relationship, which is unchanged (its accepted disclosure is not widened).

CoachProfileResponse.description:
Always returned, also before onboarding has started (`status: not_started`, every field empty), so a
client can render and resume onboarding from this response alone. Selections are always arrays.

bio.description: Optional public bio, plain text. Trimmed; up to 500 characters; line breaks allowed.
bio.example: Footwork-first boxing. I run 10-week fight camps for amateurs.

brand_name.description: Optional public coaching brand. Trimmed; 1-80 characters.

city.description: City. Trimmed; 1-80 characters. Required to complete onboarding.

coaching_formats.description:
How the coach works. Any number; a repeated value is rejected with `invalid`; `null` or `[]` clears. At least one is required to
complete onboarding, and a completed profile cannot clear them all.

competition_levels.description:
Optional competitive levels of the fighters the coach prepares (same keys as the fighter
profile's experience levels). Any number; a repeated value is rejected with `invalid`; `null` or
`[]` clears.

country_code.description:
Country as an officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (same list as the fighter profile).
Trimmed and returned in uppercase; codes that are not assigned are rejected with `invalid_choice`.
Required to complete onboarding.

display_name.description:
Public coach name. Trimmed; 1-60 characters, no control characters. Owned by the coach profile:
never copied from the account's full name or the fighter profile, and changing either never changes
it. Required to complete onboarding.

languages.description:
Languages the coach coaches in (ISO 639-1; spoken languages, not app locales). Any number; a repeated
value is rejected with `invalid`; `null` or `[]` clears.

completed_at.description: When onboarding was completed; `null` until then. Never changes afterwards.

missing_requirements.description: Required fields still empty, in step order. Completion succeeds only when this is empty.

status.description:
`not_started`: no coach profile yet. `in_progress`: progress saved, not completed (also when
every required field is present). `completed`: completion recorded by
`completeMyCoachOnboarding`.

CoachProfileResponse.title: CoachProfileResponse

outside this schema (for example `user_id`, `coach_id`, `gym_id` or `onboarding_completed_at`) is
rejected with `422 validation_error`, code `invalid` under that field name, and nothing is saved.

context.description: `fighter` or `coach`. Profile contexts only; gym workspaces are chosen elsewhere.

EntryResponse.description: Where the authenticated user goes next. `destination` is semantic: each client maps it to its own route.

capabilities.description:
Capabilities derived from real backend state, in the client route registry's vocabulary
(`FIGHTER` once Fighter onboarding is complete, `COACH` once Coach onboarding is complete; both can
be held at once). A routing projection, not an authorization grant: `COACH` opens the user's own
Coach application only.

context.description:
The requested `context` when it was applied (a completed profile, no `intent`, registration
complete); otherwise `null`. Never stored.

destination.description:
`account_registration`: shared basics and consents (mandatory). `role_selection`: the user chooses
a journey to start. `context_selection`: the user chooses between their profile contexts (both
completed without a remembered choice, or both onboardings in progress). `fighter_onboarding` /
`fighter_home` and `coach_onboarding` / `coach_home`: a profile's onboarding, or its application
once completed. `gym_onboarding`, `sponsor_application`: those journeys' entry points; nothing is
created for them. A client that does not know a destination must fail visibly, never guess.

intent.description: The validated intent of this request, echoed; never stored.

mandatory.description:
`true` when the client must go to `destination` even with a safe `returnTo` in hand (account
registration, Fighter or Coach onboarding); the `returnTo` is kept and resolved again afterwards.

reason.description: Why this destination was chosen. For diagnostics and copy, not branching.

EntryResponse.title: EntryResponse

Error.description: Machine-readable error. See the ErrorResponse schema for the contract.

example.message: The requested resource was not found

code.description:
Stable snake_case error code. Clients branch on this value, never on `message`.
New codes may be added over time; treat unknown codes according to the HTTP status.
Known codes: `bad_request`, `unauthorized`, `forbidden`, `invitation_recipient_mismatch`, `not_found`, `not_acceptable`, `conflict`, `verified_elsewhere`, `invitation_unavailable`, `payload_too_large`, `unsupported_media_type`, `validation_error`, `code_invalid`, `code_expired`, `rate_limited`, `internal_error`, `service_unavailable`.

details.description:
Code-specific structured data; an empty object when there is nothing to add.
For `validation_error` it is a `ValidationErrorDetails`: `fields` maps each invalid
field to human-readable messages and `field_codes` to the matching machine-readable
reason codes (same order).

message.description: Human-readable English summary. Not localised; may change without notice.
message.example: The requested resource was not found

request_id.description: Value of the `x-request-id` response header, for support and log correlation.

Error.title: Error

ErrorResponse.description:
Envelope returned with every 4xx and 5xx response. Stack traces and internal details
are never included.

error.message: The requested resource was not found

FighterProfileResponse.description:
Always returned, also before onboarding has started (`status: not_started`, every field empty), so a
client can render onboarding from this response alone. Body data is included only because the viewer
is the profile's owner.

amateur_bout_count.description:
Amateur bouts fought (OF2, drawn on the Competitive Amateur option). Optional and independent of
`experience_level`: changing the level keeps it.

country_code.description:
Country as an officially assigned ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code (OF1 country selector). Trimmed and returned
in uppercase; codes that are not assigned are rejected with `invalid_choice`.

current_weight_kg.description:
Current weight in kilograms with at most one decimal place (OF4, optional); more precision is rejected
with `invalid_format`, never rounded. Private. The bounds are technical
validity only, not eligibility rules.

display_name.description: Name shown to teammates and coaches (OF1). Trimmed.

goals.description: Training goals, any number, no repeats (OF3).

height_cm.description: Height in whole centimetres (OF4, optional). Private. Technical bounds only.

next_fight_name.description: Event of the next fight (OF3, optional). Independent of `next_fight_on`.

next_fight_on.description: Date of the next fight (OF3, optional).

completed_at.description: When onboarding was completed; `null` until then.

missing_requirements.description: Required fields still empty, in step order. Completion succeeds only when this is empty.

status.description:
`not_started`: no fighter profile yet. `in_progress`: progress saved, not completed.
`completed`: completion recorded by `completeFighterOnboarding`.

username.description:
Unique handle without the `@` (OF1). Trimmed and stored in lowercase: 3-30 ASCII letters, digits or
underscores, starting and ending with a letter or digit. Uniqueness ignores case; a handle another
fighter holds is rejected with `already_exists`.

weight_class.description:
Approximate weight class in kg (OF4): `minus_63_5` is −63.5, `plus_86` is +86. Private: never shown
to other users.

public identity and note; never the token, the address it was sent to or anything about other accounts.

the text (`title`, `summary`, `checkbox`, `full`) only when an approved variant exists in exactly the

one to echo as `document_language` when accepting); `null` with no text. Render `summary`, `checkbox`
and `full` as plain text or the Markdown subset (headings, paragraphs, `-` lists); never as HTML.

status.description: Only `published` can be accepted; `superseded` is an archive.

version.description: The version id; one id covers all languages.

ValidationErrorDetails.description:
`details` of a `validation_error`. Both maps have the same keys (field names; nested
fields use dotted paths such as `address.city`) and, per field, the same number of entries
in the same order: `field_codes[field][i]` is the reason for `fields[field][i]`.
Clients branch on `field_codes`, never on the messages in `fields`. New reason codes may
be added; treat unknown ones as `invalid`.

field_codes.description: Field name to stable machine-readable reason codes.

fields.description: Field name to human-readable messages (English, for display and debugging).

refreshCookie.description:

info.description:
Backend API for SimpleFit Boxing: the operating system and professional network for boxing.

## Conventions

* JSON request and response bodies (`application/json`) only.
* Errors use a single envelope (`ErrorResponse`) with a stable machine-readable `code`;
  validation errors add per-field reason codes (`ValidationErrorDetails`). Clients branch
  on codes, never on human-readable messages.
* Browser clients must be on the API's CORS allow-list (explicit origins, no wildcard).
* Every response carries an `x-request-id` header; error bodies echo it as `request_id`.
* Product resources will be served under `/api/v1`. Operational, session (`/api/auth`) and viewer
  (`/api/me`) endpoints live under `/api`.
* Authenticated endpoints take `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`; see `SessionTokens`.
info.title: SimpleFit API

post.description:
Verifies the Apple identity token (RS256 signature with Apple's keys, issuer, audience, expiry, subject, and
the nonce: the token's `nonce` must be the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw `nonce` sent here) and starts a
SimpleFit session. Apple credentials are never SimpleFit credentials and are not stored.

The Apple account is identified only by its subject (`sub`): an unknown one creates a new account
(`account: created`), a known one signs in (`account: existing`). Email (including private relay
addresses) and name are never read; accounts are never linked by email.

* `unauthorized` - the token is not a valid Apple identity token for SimpleFit (no detail is given).
* `service_unavailable` - Apple's signing keys cannot be obtained or Sign in with Apple is not configured.

parameters.name: x-simplefit-csrf

post.description:
Starts the email ownership verification of a new account and sends E01 (a 6-digit code and a verification
link). Requesting again for the same address replaces the previous code, link and registration token.

The response is the same for every well-formed address, including addresses that already have an account
(no email is sent then, and nothing is created): it never reveals whether an account exists. Sign-up never
turns into sign-in.

post.description:
Verifies the email of a registration with the 6-digit code from E01. Only the client that started the
registration can do this: it sends its `registration_token`. On success the account exists and this client
receives the registration's one SF-20 session.

* `code_invalid` - wrong code. After 5 wrong codes the code stops working.
* `code_expired` - the code expired, was replaced, was already used or stopped working: request a new one.
* `verified_elsewhere` - the email was verified through the E01 link (possibly on another device). The link
  never signs anyone in: this client must sign in with an email sign-in code.
* `conflict` - the address already has an account.

post.description:
Verifies the Google ID token (RS256 signature with Google's keys, issuer, audience, authorized party, expiry,
subject) and starts a SimpleFit session. The Google token is never a SimpleFit credential and is not stored.

The Google account is identified only by its subject (`sub`): an unknown one creates a new account
(`account: created`), a known one signs in (`account: existing`). Accounts are never linked by email.

* `unauthorized` - the token is not a valid Google ID token for SimpleFit (no detail is given).
* `service_unavailable` - Google's signing keys cannot be obtained or Google sign-in is not configured.

post.description:
Revokes the session identified by the request's credential: the bearer access token, the refresh
token in the body, or the web refresh cookie (cookie requests need an allow-listed `Origin` and
`x-simplefit-csrf: 1`). The refresh cookie is always cleared.

Idempotent: the response is `204` whether the session was active, already revoked or not
identifiable, so it reveals nothing about any session. A revoked session can no longer refresh or
access authenticated endpoints.

parameters.description: Required (value `1`) when the refresh token is sent as the web cookie, together with an allow-listed `Origin`.
parameters.name: x-simplefit-csrf

204.description: Logged out (or nothing to log out)

set-cookie.description: Cookie transport only: the rotated refresh token (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/auth`) or its deletion.

post.summary: Log out of the current session

post.description:
Consumes the refresh token and issues a new access token and a new refresh token for the same
session. A refresh token works once: presenting a consumed token again revokes its session,
except to recover a lost response: until the new refresh token is first used, the previous one
can be presented again for a short time, which replaces the unused new token (ADR 0010).

**Transport** (exactly one):

* Mobile/body: send `{"refresh_token": "sfr_..."}`; the new refresh token is returned in the body.
* Web/cookie: send the `__Secure-sf_refresh` cookie (no body token), an allow-listed `Origin` and
  `x-simplefit-csrf: 1`; the new refresh token is set as the cookie and omitted from the body.

Every invalid, expired, revoked or reused token yields the same `401 unauthorized` (and, for the
cookie transport, clears the cookie).

parameters.name: x-simplefit-csrf

get.description:
Returns the shared account registration: basics, consent state and the missing requirements. Before
registration has started the response is still `200` with `status: not_started`; reading creates nothing.
Authentication never completes registration, whatever the sign-in method.

patch.description:
Saves any subset of the basics and consent decisions. The first save that persists something creates the
account profile (`in_progress`); a save with nothing to persist creates nothing. Required consents are
recorded with their current document version; product news can be subscribed and withdrawn. An invalid
request changes nothing.

post.description:
Records that shared account registration is complete, after checking every requirement on the server: full
name, a date of birth at least 16 years ago, and current acceptance of the Terms of Service and the Privacy
Policy. While anything is missing the response is `422 validation_error` with a `required` field code per
missing item (`full_name`, `date_of_birth`, `terms`, `privacy`) and nothing changes. Completion is
permanent: completing again returns the state with the original `completed_at`, and a later Terms or
Privacy version change does not reopen it (`consents.*.current` reports it instead).

get.description:
The invitations sent to any email identity the viewer verified with a code, newest first, with the coach's
public identity and note and the effective status. Matched on the server from the session's user: no
address, user id or provider email is accepted, and Google or Apple sign-ins without an email identity have
an empty inbox. Nothing here is a relationship (see `listMyCoaches`); respond with the invitation link
(`acceptCoachInvitation`, `declineCoachInvitation`) or by id (`acceptMyIncomingCoachInvitation`,
`declineMyIncomingCoachInvitation`). Other query parameters are ignored.

* `not_found` - Coach–Fighter sharing is not enabled (distinct from an empty inbox).
* `validation_error` - `account_registration` `required`, or `limit`, `cursor` or `status` invalid.

parameters.name: status

parameters.description: Page size, 1-100 (default 50).
parameters.name: limit

parameters.description: `next_cursor` of the previous page (same `status`).
parameters.name: cursor

post.description:
The explicit acceptance. The viewer must be signed in with the invited address (an email identity they
verified), have completed account registration and a fighter profile, and echo exactly the disclosure version
shown by `previewCoachInvitation`. In one transaction the invitation is consumed and the relationship becomes
active with that disclosure; nothing changes if any step fails. A token works once: a repeated acceptance
answers `410` (see `listMyCoaches`).

* `invitation_unavailable` (410) - not a current pending invitation, or the viewer's own.
* `invitation_recipient_mismatch` (403) - the viewer is not signed in with the invited address.
* `validation_error` - `account_registration` or `fighter_profile` `required`; `coaching_age` `too_young`
  (Coach–Fighter connections need the fighter to be 18 or older; the coach is never told); or
  `disclosure_version` / `document_language` missing.
* `conflict` - `disclosure_version` is not the current version (details `disclosure_version: stale`), or
  `document_language` has no approved disclosure text (`document_language: unavailable`).
* `not_found` - Coach–Fighter sharing is not available (gate off or no published documents).
* `rate_limited` - 30 per 10 minutes per client.

On success the relationship, the consumed invitation and the evidence of the acceptance (version, language,
text hash) commit together.

retry-after.description: Seconds until another request is accepted.

post.description:
The explicit decline: by the viewer signed in with the invited address and with a completed fighter profile.
Creates nothing; the link stops working. Also available while Coach–Fighter sharing is not enabled.

* `invitation_unavailable` (410), `invitation_recipient_mismatch` (403), `validation_error`
  (`account_registration` / `fighter_profile` `required`) - as for `acceptCoachInvitation`.
* `rate_limited` - 30 per 10 minutes per client.

* `rate_limited` - 30 per 10 minutes per client.

(`in_progress`). Values are validated but nothing is required until completion, and saving never
completes onboarding. A field outside `CoachProfileUpdateRequest` (including ids, the owner and the

(`completeAccountRegistration`): until then the error carries `account_registration` with code `required`.
Completing again returns the profile with its original `completed_at`. Completion grants no access to
other users' data.

post.description:
Invites an email address to connect with the viewer as their coach and sends E08 with a one-time link
(14 days). Creates no account, profile or relationship: only the recipient, signed in with that address,
can accept. A pending invitation of the viewer to the same address is returned unchanged (`200`, no new
email). Answers the same whether or not the address has an account.

* `conflict` - the coach data rules are not acknowledged (`data_rules_acknowledgement: required`), or 50
  invitations are pending (`pending_invitations: limit_reached`).
* `not_found` - sharing is not enabled, no disclosure version is configured, or no completed coach profile.
* `validation_error` - `email` missing, malformed or the viewer's own; `message` too long or not one plain
  paragraph; any other field.
* `rate_limited` - per coach (10/hour, 30/day), per recipient (3/day) or per client (20 per 10 minutes).

  (`resends: limit_reached`).
* `rate_limited` - within 60 seconds of the last send, or the coach's hourly limit.
* `not_found` - unknown or someone else's invitation, sharing not enabled, or no completed coach profile.

get.description:
Resolves where the authenticated user should go next, as a semantic destination that each client maps to its
own route (never a path). The answer is derived from current state on every call and resolving writes nothing,
so repeated and concurrent calls are safe and advance on their own as registration and onboarding complete.

Order (ADR 0017 as amended by SF-51): mandatory account registration first; then an explicit `intent`
(`fighter` / `coach` lead to that profile's home when completed, otherwise to its onboarding, whatever the
other profile's state; `gym` / `sponsor` to their entry points); then a requested `context` that names a
completed profile; otherwise the default by completed profiles: none - resume the one onboarding in progress
or choose (`role_selection`, or `context_selection` when both are in progress); one - its home; both - the
last context chosen with `chooseMyEntryContext`, or `context_selection`. `intent` and `context` are navigation
only and grant nothing; `capabilities` projects completed profiles for routing and is not an authorization
grant.

* `validation_error` - `intent` or `context` is not one of the allowed values (`invalid_choice`).

parameters.description: The journey the user explicitly tried to enter. Omit when there is none.
parameters.name: intent

parameters.description:
An application context to open. Used only when that profile is completed (otherwise ignored, and it never
starts onboarding); ignored when `intent` is present. Never stored: see `chooseMyEntryContext`.
parameters.name: context

put.description:
Records an explicit choice between the viewer's completed profile contexts (a context switcher or the
context-selection screen). With both Fighter and Coach completed and no `intent` or `context`, the entry then
resolves to this context's home. Only a completed context can be chosen; the latest choice replaces the
previous one, from any device. A navigation preference, never an authorization grant: it is re-checked on
every resolution. Resolving the entry never records a choice.

* `conflict` - that profile context is not completed; nothing is recorded.
* `validation_error` - `context` is missing (`required`) or not an allowed value (`invalid_choice`); any
  other field is rejected with `invalid` under its name.
put.summary: Remember the application context I chose

get.description:
Whether the viewer should be offered each one-time first-run experience. Derived on every call from the
recorded outcome and the viewer's current state; reading creates nothing. Completing an onboarding never
records an outcome: a newly onboarded Fighter's tour is `pending`.

put.description:
Records that the viewer finished (`completed`) or ended (`dismissed`) the experience, after which it is never
offered again on any client. The first outcome is final: repeating the request, or sending the other outcome
(another tab or device), returns the kept outcome with its original `recorded_at`.

* `not_found` - unknown experience.
* `conflict` - the experience is `unavailable` to the viewer (for the Fighter experiences, Fighter
  onboarding is not complete); nothing is recorded.
* `validation_error` - `outcome` is missing (`required`) or not an allowed value (`invalid_choice`).
